newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says wants critical dialogue with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Italy says wants critical dialogue with Iran.

text.p: Italy said on Wednesday it wanted to pursue a "critical dialogue" with Iran despite a European Union decision to stop such talks with the Islamic nation.

"We want to continue a critical dialogue with Iraq, Iran and Libya which does not at all distance us from our tight alliances, especially with the United States. Marginalisation is not useful," Prime Minister Romano Prodi told reporters after a speech to foreign ambassadors in Italy.

The EU halted its policy of critical dialogue with Iran in April after a German court implicated Tehran in the killing of Iranian Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. The EU's 15 nations also withdrew their ambassadors from Iran.

The policy, under which the EU talked to Iran while making it clear the bloc disapproved of Tehran's international stance, had long been at odds with the U.S. approach of isolating Iran as a "rogue" nation.
